missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Хвост' stays in the nominative as the subject of the sentence. 'Длинный' and 'пушистый' are agreeing masculine adjectives, and 'у кошки' shows whose tail it is.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Хвостом' is the instrumental case, showing the instrument of the action 'виляет'. 'От радости' adds the cause, a very natural everyday image.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Хвост' is the accusative direct object of 'поднял'; for inanimate masculine nouns the accusative matches the nominative. 'И убежал' continues the action.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Хвоста' is the genitive case required after 'нет' to express that something is missing. A core pattern for stating what is absent.
Strategic focus: Accusative with 'за'. 'Хвост' is the accusative object after 'за', expressing what is held. 'Лошади' is genitive showing whose tail. A natural spatial scene.
Strategic focus: Prepositional of location. 'На хвосте' uses the prepositional form 'хвосте' after 'на' to mark location. 'Сидит' agrees with the feminine subject 'бабочка'.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Хвостом' is instrumental, the tool of the motion 'махнула'. 'И нырнула' chains a second action, modelling lively narration.
Strategic focus: Accusative object with dative recipient. 'Хвост' is the accusative object of 'нарисовал', while 'коту' is the dative beneficiary. 'Пушистый' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Хвосты' is the nominative plural subject. 'Красивые' is the agreeing plural adjective, and 'у павлинов' marks the possessors in the genitive plural.
Strategic focus: Prepositional plural. 'О хвостах' uses the prepositional plural after 'о' to mark the topic of conversation. 'Животных' is genitive plural showing whose tails.
